QF.id: SIA Assessment Frameworks Techniques and Standards_1

question.text: Ms. Sunita Patil (SIA) is scoping an impact evaluation for Pragati Foundation, an education NPO listed on NSE-SSE. The SE's management asks her to use a framework that emphasises underlying causal pathways, tests assumptions, and captures contextual factors rather than a simple linear input-output diagram. Which framework best fits this requirement?

answer.text: Logic Model — because it visually depicts inputs, activities, outputs and outcomes in a sequential linear diagram
Theory of Change (ToC) — because it is narrative-driven, highlights causal pathways, and explicitly tests assumptions against context
GIIRS rating model — because it gives a composite score comparable to Morningstar
GRI Universal Standards — because they disclose sector-agnostic organisational policies

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 6 contrasts ToC with the Logic Model: ToC is narrative-driven, highlights causal links between activities/intermediate outcomes/long-term outcomes, explicitly tests underlying assumptions, and considers broader context. The Logic Model is linear and less flexible. For an education NPO where Sunita must probe assumptions (e.g., parents will allow girls to attend), ToC is the right fit. The Trap: Logic Model shares the cause-effect idea but stops at a linear diagram. GIIRS is a rating system (not a planning framework). GRI is a disclosure/reporting standard, not a causal-pathway tool. Cross-Exam Context: Cross-refers to XXIII Ch 5 (Theory of Change deep dive) and SAS-100 engagement planning where the SIA must document the SE's ToC. XV Research Analyst exams use logic trees too but for thesis building, not impact. Assessor's Pro-Tip: When kicking off a SAS-100 engagement, ask the SE for its written ToC first — if they only have a Logic Model, rebuild the causal pathway with them during the planning phase so assumption-testing is baked into your evidence plan.
